p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration outlining the fate of the glucose carbons in the formation of glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. At the top is fructose 1,6-bisphosphate which begins with 1CH2, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. CH2 also bonds down to 2C, which double bonds right to O and down to 3C, which bonds right to H and left to HO. This is all in a pink box. C also bonds down to 4C, which bonds right to OH, left to H, and down to 5C, which bonds right to OH, left to H, and down to 6CH2, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. This is all in a blue box. Below this and to the left is a pink box with dihydroxyacetone phosphate, where CH2 bonds right to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. CH2 also bonds down to C, which double bonds right to O and bonds down to CH2OH. To the right of this is a blue box for glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate, where C double bonds right to O, bonds left to H, and down to C, which bonds right to OH, left to H, and down to CH2, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. The pink and blue boxes each have double-ended arrows that merge pointing up to fructose 1,6-bisphosphate. To the left of this arrow is aldolase in blue. Below the pink and blue boxes are curved reversible arrows, with triose phosphate isomerase in blue below them. To the left of the pink box are the numbers 1, 2, and 3. They line up with each bonding line in the pink box. Above them, it states, “Derived from glucose carbon.” To the right of the blue box are the numbers 4, 5, and 6. They line up as described above. Above them, it states, “Derived from glucose carbon.” To the right is D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. It begins with 1C, which double bonds right to O, bonds left to H, and down to 2C, which bonds right to OH, left to H, and down to 3CH2, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to P in a circle. To the left of this are numbers in three lines that line up with the bonding lines in D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. On the first line is 4 or 3, on the second line is 5 or 2, and on the third line is 6 or 1. Above these it states, “Derived from glucose carbons.” Below D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate is an arrow pointing down to subsequent reactions of glycolysis.
